note.seg: Vielleicht las das Original Angolwitena (s. V Atr Insc.) gerædnes; Q jedenfalls erfand das überflüssige Anglie nicht und hätte den Königsnamen hinzugesetzt
Perhaps the original read Angolwitena (see V Atr Insc.) gerædnes; Q at any rate did not invent the superfluous Anglie, and would have added the king's name

Die Rubrikenliste, nur in jüngster Q-Rezension, stammt vielleicht überall nur aus dem Latein. Texte, verfehlt in c. 5 den Sinn, verbindet fälschlich 6, 3 mit 6, 4f. und bildet aus 6, 6f. ein besonderes Kapitel

The rubric list, found only in the latest recension of Q, perhaps derives throughout solely from the Latin text; it misses the sense in c. 5, wrongly joins 6, 3 with 6, 4f., and makes a separate chapter out of 6, 6f.

This fragment is found only in H, where it is appended to V As. It differs considerably from the Latin text. In § 1 the bishop is placed alongside the king as being able to grant a respite of nine days (see note to IV As. 6 § 2)—a privilege granted only to the archbishop in the Latin version. There is nothing in the Latin version corresponding to § 3, and this, with the comparative mildness of the punishment (cf. Alf. cap. 2 § 1, II Edm. cap. 4), suggests that § 3 is a later insertion. For a discussion of the relationship between the Latin and A.S. texts see Liebermann, iii. p. 112.
